FROMLIST: ASoC: SOF: Add direction param in cmd_done There are two direction now in cmd_done, one is reply of host to DSP, another is reply of DSP to host.The origin cmd_done is for reply of host to DSP. Cmd_done should be called after host has processed the reply msg from dsp. This function is for some platforms to do extra steps to make the following ipc msgs sent safely. Now the direction supported by cmd_done would be host reply to dsp or dsp reply to host. Signed-off-by: Rander Wang <rander.wang@linux.intel.com> (cherry picked from commit ed5707d912c1a4165f7bbd66fd651f72ed6ff6ec) Link:https://github.com/thesofproject/linux/commit/ed5707d912c1a4165f7bbd66fd651f72ed6ff6ec Signed-off-by: Samaga Prasanna Krishna <samaga.krishna@intel.corp-partner.google.com> BUG=b:110025789 TEST=Test Audio use cases after full SOF series patches are applied. Change-Id: I3ed21097939e0e8bb56e202e01c2127d6c78b3b7 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1163300 Commit-Ready: Curtis Malainey <cujomalainey@chromium.org> Tested-by: Curtis Malainey <cujomalainey@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Curtis Malainey <cujomalainey@chromium.org>

FROMLIST: ASoC: SOF: check is_dsp_ready when sending ipc msg Refine the implementation of is_dsp_ready on APL&CNL BUSY bit means dsp is ready, DONE bit means host has processed the reply msg. CHROMIUM: ASoC: SOF: remove superfluous parent device pointers of snd_sof_pdata We had pointers for parent device of snd_sof_pdata, pci for pci_dev, pdev for platform_device, and spi for spi_device (intended to but not added yet). All of these can be retrieved from parent dev via container_of(), so they are actually superfluous. Here remove these pointers to kinds of parent devices, add an enum sof_device_type and simplify the initialization of snd_sof_dev->parent correspondingly. Signed-off-by: Keyon Jie <yang.jie@linux.intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 54fe2635d99214f72a6da05529b90c687a5cdc51) BUG=b:110025789 TEST=Test Audio use cases after full SOF series patches are applied. cellular: give ServiceAutoConnectContext some time to find cellular service As some tests may disable the cellular device, it may take some time before the cellular service to reappear after the cellular device is re-enabled. This CL updates cellular tests to use CellularProxy.wait_for_cellular_service_object, instead of CellularProxy.get_cellular_service_object, to give ServiceAutoConnectContext some time to wait for a cellular service to re-appear. BUG=None TEST=Run cellular_qual test suites. add platform.Memd tast-test This test checks that memd is running and responding to events of interest by creating clip files. The events of interest are faked. A tab discard is simulated by sending a D-Bus message that looks as if it came from Chrome. A kernel OOM kill is simulated by producing a syslog line that is recognized by the anomaly_collector daemon. Thus this also tests the OOM-kill reporting functionality of the anomaly collector. BUG=chromium:900291 TEST=ran the test CQ-DEPEND=CL:1308497,CL:1308673 Change-Id: Ibd278e4afe346dacd3ac37f8b10ce5a62d00a445 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1306913 Commit-Ready: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org> Tested-by: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Luigi Semenzato <semenzato@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

dt_set_macs: Add support for colons in MAC addresses Turns out that our VPD specification actually requires colons in the MAC address field. Storm and Gale apparently didn't do that, but it seems better to follow the spec we have going forward. This patch updates the MAC address decode code to work on both versions with and without colons. BRANCH=None BUG=b:118837709 TEST=Ran through the code with GDB and confirmed fields with and without colons in them were correctly decoded. Change-Id: I0a55c70cacd5c86d9970338861918f9d0bc388a2 Signed-off-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1313231 Reviewed-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>
